instrument: Virginia Data Center Accountability Framework (proposed; 2027 General Assembly legislative agenda)
section: Increase Transparency and End the Secrecy
summary: Proposes to ban NDAs for commercial data center projects, eliminate by-right approval and require local approval of any data center using more than 25 MW, end state site-development subsidies, and remove future large data centers from fast-track permitting.
text: Ban non-disclosure agreements for commercial data center projects; Strengthen local control by eliminating by-right approval and requiring local approval of any data center using more than 25 megawatts of power; Empower communities with tools to negotiate stronger, community-centered agreements; End state subsidies for data centers in Virginia's site development programs; Remove future large data centers from Virginia's fast-track permitting process

source.citation: Office of the Governor of Virginia, news release, Governor Spanberger Unveils Nation's Most Comprehensive & Aggressive Data Center Accountability Standards, Signs Executive Order to Immediately Put Into Action, September 18, 2026

notes: These are the provisions widely reported as effective under EO 22. The NDA ban reaching commercial projects and the 25 MW local-approval requirement are Framework proposals; EO 22 implements only the executive-branch NDA prohibition and the VEDP exclusion.
confidence_note: Read in original from the Governor's release, which lists the Framework's contents. The Framework document itself was not opened (link behind a redirect). Framework items are proposals for the 2027 General Assembly and are NOT in force except where Executive Order 22 implements them; see the us-va-state EO 22 entries.
